messages:
AcmeDev: Hey team — since last night we're seeing a sudden burst of 429s hitting rwd-3-large when our background prefetch job runs. It started after we increased fanout to ~200 parallel fetches. Example header from one failed call: 
Request-ID: acme-req-9921, status: 429, body: {"error":"rate_limited"}

Alice (Support): sorry to hear that, can you paste a minimal curl + headers you used and the approximate request rate (req/min) and tokens per request? Also, are these streaming requests or normal responses?

AcmeDev: Curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \u005C
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXX' \u005C
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \u005C
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3-large","input":"<prefetch payload...>","max_tokens":4096,"context_length":65536}'
```
Rate: ~180 req/min by one worker pool, each request pulls ~25k tokens (avg). Non-streaming. Failures appear after sustained 60s.

Brian (SRE): Thanks — that pattern (high fanout + large context) is classic per-model quota exhaustion. For rwd-3-large your project is hitting two soft caps we enforce: per-model requests/min (RPM) and token/min (TPM). Also there's a practical max concurrency per model instance. When the system sees sustained burst above the RPM or TPM windows it returns 429s and starts shedding requests.

Brian (SRE): Quick numbers from our side (approx for your tenant): the configured per-model RPM ~= 120, TPM ~= 250000 tokens/min, and effective max concurrency ~= 12 for rwd-3-large. Your pattern (~180 rpm * ~25k tokens) >> TPM and spikes concurrency.

AcmeDev: Ok that math makes sense. Is the token accounting including context + generated tokens? We're sending large context but generating ~500 tokens only.

Priya (Eng): Token accounting = context tokens + response tokens. So a 25k context + 500 generated = 25.5k counted. Large contexts are expensive for TPM. Also: long-context requests have additional cost on concurrency because of KV cache warmup and memory reservations, which reduce effective concurrent slots.

AcmeDev: Any repro steps we can run to validate? Want to reproduce locally before changing prod.

Brian (SRE): Repro recipe: start 1 worker that launches 200 async tasks across 5 minutes, each task does a single POST to rwd-3-large with a 24k-token context. Track 429 rate. Example load script (simplified):
```python
# pseudocode
for i in range(200):
  spawn(thread) -> requests.post(... huge_context ...)
```
Wait ~60-90s and you'll see 429s. On our tier, you'll exceed TPM first, then concurrent queueing.

AcmeDev: We ran that and got 30% 429s within 90s. Any config tweaks we can apply quickly?

Alice (Support): Short-term mitigations: 1) reduce prefetch fanout (e.g., 50 concurrent), 2) stagger jobs with jitter, 3) implement exponential backoff with Retry-After handling, 4) cache embeddings/headers to avoid re-sending full context if you can.

Priya (Eng): Code snippet for backoff (JS style):
```js
async function callWithBackoff(req){
  let attempt=0;
  while(attempt<6){
    const res = await fetch(...);
    if(res.status!==429) return res;
    const ra = res.headers.get('retry-after') || Math.pow(2,attempt)*100;
    await sleep(ra);
    attempt++
  }
  throw new Error('rate-limited');
}
```

AcmeDev: Billing question — will the failed 429 requests still charge tokens? We're seeing a billing spike.

billing-bot: Failed 429 responses do not bill for generated tokens if generation did not start; however context tokens and partial compute may be accounted in some internal meters. I'll pull the finer details soon — please share a few request IDs (e.g., acme-req-9921, acme-req-9940).

AcmeDev: Posted a small sample of request IDs in a DM to @Alice.

Alice (Support): Received. I opened a ticket for a temporary throttle increase while you refactor prefetching: ticket RED-4451. We'll monitor for 12 hours. In parallel, please try the mitigations above.

Brian (SRE): Long-term options: 1) move heavy prefetch to Redwood Dedicated or Private so you can reserve capacity, 2) use a model variant explicitly built for 64k contexts (if available in your catalog) which has different concurrency/PTM profiles, or 3) rearchitect to incremental chunked fetch + rolling window.

AcmeDev: If we move to Dedicated, will the concurrency/TPM guarantees change?

Priya (Eng): Dedicated pools give you reserved slots and higher per-model effective throughput; we can size a pool based on your sustained tokens/min. That avoids the shared per-model RPM/TPM throttles. We'll need usage projections.

AcmeDev: Thanks — we'll try reducing fanout + backoff and report. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy status: created support/temporary-throttle-bump RED-4451 -> applied to tenant acme (12h) :white_check_mark:

Alice (Support): Leaving this thread open. If you still see 429s after the mitigations + temporary bump, ping us and we'll collect traces and escalate to runtime ops.
